marks.gloss_en: סיפא ודאי מסייעא ליה: 'from so-and-so' -- he is believed
the same mishna's seifa: [if he said] 'from so-and-so' -- he is believed
התם כיון דאית ליה תובע מירתת -- there, since he has a claimant, he is afraid

Ravina to Rav Ashi: perhaps it is an Israelite, and Rav Yehuda said one does not examine an Israelite's firstborn unless a priest is with him! (an amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest)
Rav Yehuda: one does not examine an Israelite's firstborn unless a priest is with him

הכי השתא -- there he is suspect about the priest's money; here, bringing a clear blemish before the Rabbis is for the Sage's honour, and one who keeps the Sage's honour will not commit a prohibition (36b.11-12; = p_ashi_chashud_mamon_kohen, p_ashi_kevod_chacham)
Rav Ashi: there, granted he does not eat sacred meat outside, he is suspect about the priest's money
והלכתא אפילו כלישנא קמא -- the halakha is even as the first version (the priest too is believed)
R' Yirmeya bar Abba: this is what I said [to Giddul]: an Israelite is believed to say 'I gave this firstborn to a priest with its blemish'
[the Israelite is believed] even where [the firstborn] was small and grew -- lest you say he does not know it for sure

Rafram in Pumbedita gave an unblemished firstborn to a priest; the priest made a blemish in it, brought it before Rafram and said 'an Israelite gave me this firstborn with its blemish'; Rafram forced his eyes open, recognised it, and said: was it not I who gave it to you?
and even so, [Rafram] was not concerned about the matter
Rav Ashi on a sarua brought before him: what should we be concerned about? whether it is a priest or an Israelite, here is a firstborn with its blemish with it
Rav Ashi: here, since he knows this is a clear blemish, why did they bring it before the Rabbis? for the Sage's honour; [one who] does not neglect the Sage's honour -- will he commit a prohibition?

מי ידע הי נפיק? -- does he know which one will come out [tenth], that he could blemish it beforehand? (and the escape 'he brings it out at the head of ten' is closed by לא יבקר, 36b.15); unanswered -- the reason is replaced (אלא)
the reason: had he wanted, he could have put a blemish in it from the start
the mishna: all are believed about the blemishes of [animal] tithe
(entertained) he brings it out [deliberately] at the head of ten
the permitting of a firstborn outside the Land is on the word of three congregants
three permit the firstborn in a place where there is no expert
where there is no expert, yes; where there is an expert, no
Rav Chiyya bar Amram: three permit the firstborn in a place where there is no expert
R' Yosei (the mishna, 36b.16; out of span, rule 13): even if twenty-three are there, only on the word of an expert
